title: South Lhonak GLOF — Teesta III Dam Failure
hazard: Moraine collapse → GLOF → dam failure → multihazard cascade
region: South Lhonak Lake → Teesta River, Mangan & Pakyong Districts, Sikkim
detectedChange: Frozen lateral moraine collapsed into South Lhonak Lake; terminal moraine breached
changePct: ≈50 million m³ of lake water drained
summary: On 3 October 2023 about 14.7 million m³ of frozen lateral moraine collapsed into South Lhonak Lake at 5,200 m. The impact generated an approximately 20 m tsunami-like wave, breached the terminal moraine and drained around 50 million m³ of water. The flood eroded roughly 270 million m³ of sediment on its way down and reached the 1,200 MW Teesta III dam at Chungthang at about 00:30 IST on 4 October, before the gates could be opened; the 60 m dam was destroyed in minutes, adding its stored water to the flood. The surge travelled 385 km down the Teesta into Bangladesh.

mparams.label: Glacier Geometry
mparams.source: Raj et al. via the Geosystems and Geoenvironment review: the glacier retreated ≈2 km over 46 years and a further ≈400 m from 2008 to 2019 — verified as published. Area figure approximate.

mparams.label: Ice / Snow
mparams.source: Science (2025) multihazard-cascade paper for 14.7 million m³; Scientific Reports (Mohanty et al.) for the ≈38.31 million m³ debris and ≈7 million m³ calving estimates — both verified as published; the estimates differ between studies.

mparams.label: Crack & Instability
mparams.source: Science (2025) for the ≈20 m impact wave and ≈270 million m³ erosion; Sattar et al. (2025) modelling via Petley's Landslide Blog for the ≈11 m peak 1 km downstream — verified as published.

mparams.label: Glacial Lakes
mparams.source: Science (2025) for the ≈50 million m³ drained and the 5,200 m elevation — verified. Pre-event area is an approximate inventory-scale figure; imagery shows water remaining after the GLOF.

mparams.label: Hydrology
mparams.source: Petley's Landslide Blog / Eos for the 00:30 arrival; Science (2025) for the 385 km path; Scientific Reports and Wikipedia for the 15–20 ft downstream rise — verified as published. Distance to the dam is quoted as ≈60, 65 or 68 km in different studies.

mparams.label: Weather / Climate
mparams.source: Intense antecedent rainfall exceeding 200 mm is reported as having destabilised the moraine slope; a cloudburst contribution is proposed in the Geosystems and Geoenvironment study. Studies disagree on how much rainfall mattered. Temperature anomaly is approximate.

mparams.label: Terrain
mparams.source: Science (2025) attributes severity partly to the massive amount of eroded material and the narrow valley with recent construction — verified narrative; slope value approximate.

mparams.label: Infrastructure
mparams.source: Eos/Petley for the 60 m dam height; Government of Sikkim (8 Nov 2023) for 16 bridges and the ≈5.08 million m³ release; Scientific Reports for 13 bridges and ≈1,200 residences — verified as reported; counts differ between sources.

mparams.label: Exposure
mparams.source: Science (2025) reports 55 deaths and 74 missing in Sikkim; the Government of Sikkim reported 42 dead, >77 missing, 88,400 affected, 5,665 evacuated and 2,563 rescued as of 8 Nov 2023 — both verified as reported on their respective dates.

mparams.label: Response Resources
mparams.source: Government of Sikkim relief figures (8 Nov 2023) and contemporaneous reporting (Sikkim Express via Penn State IEE) — verified as reported.
